quarterly_data.signal: CFO Stefano Beretta: Q2 2026 revenue was an all-time record, exceeding EUR 277 million and above the high end of the outlook range, up 64.3% year over year and more than 48% sequentially versus Q1 2026; gross profit EUR 158.5 million (57.2% margin, above the high end of the outlook); EBITDA EUR 137 million, up 135% year over year, margin over 49%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue > EUR 277 million, +64.3% YoY; gross margin 57.2%; EBITDA EUR 137 million (+135% YoY, margin over 49%)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (CEO Stefano Felici, CFO Stefano Beretta): record revenue of EUR 464.1 million, up 42.4% year over year; gross profit EUR 249.6 million, up 65.7%, gross margin 53.8% (from 46.2%, +760 bp); EBITDA EUR 206.2 million, margin 44.4%. Growth was organic (almost EUR 170 million), largely sustained by AI volumes plus a soft recovery in consumer and a slight recovery in automotive and industrial; FX headwind of approximately EUR 30 million on revenue (more than 6%) and approximately EUR 23 million at EBITDA level. About EUR 93 million of operating cash was practically all used to fund the capacity expansion; net financial position almost stable.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue EUR 464.1 million (+42.4% YoY); gross margin 53.8%; EBITDA EUR 206.2 million (44.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (CFO): Q3 2026 expected to be another sequential record, revenue about EUR 314 million +/-3%, gross margin about 61.5% +/-200 bp, EBITDA margin about 52% +/-200 bp. FY2026 targets revised upwards again: consolidated revenue EUR 1,050 million to EUR 1,100 million, EBITDA margin 46% to 48%. CFO: Q4 still under examination with short visibility; Q4 revenue currently expected in a range between Q2 and Q3 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 revenue ~EUR 314 million +/-3%; FY2026 revenue EUR 1,050 million to EUR 1,100 million, EBITDA margin 46% to 48%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity expansion (CFO): total investment to be deployed January 2026 to March 2027 raised from EUR 250 million to approximately EUR 350 million; approximately EUR 90 million spent by end of June 2026, about EUR 250 million left for the next nine months (mostly machinery and equipment, depending on supplier deliveries; some could slip one or two months). The extra EUR 100 million is almost entirely equipment and automation, in Italy and also in Taiwan, Korea and China. Capacity target raised from a EUR 1.4 billion run rate to at least a EUR 1.6 billion run rate at end of Q1 2027 (1.9 in USD), up to 140% above the end-2025 run rate. About 80% of the investment is in Italy, where a new 4,000 sq m greenfield manufacturing facility in Cernusco Lombardone is under construction, to be completed by end of Q1 2027; capacity from process optimisation is expected to rise month by month through end-2026. CFO expects the capacity to be largely used by end of Q1 and to serve all main customers barring unexpected events such as HBM or silicon photonics adoption.
quarterly_data.figure: investment ~EUR 350 million (from EUR 250 million) Jan 2026 to Mar 2027; capacity run rate EUR 1.6 billion (from EUR 1.4 billion) by end Q1 2027; up to 140% vs end-2025

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: expects another significant round of investment for 2027 and 2028, amount and timing still to be discussed and approved by the board; capacity will increase gradually all over 2027 under a preliminary investment plan. CEO: investment planning is based on quarterly feedback from the major customers and foundries, which give good visibility (not orders or commitments).

Product mix (CFO): the GPU mass-production campaigns that drove H1 growth are expected to pause in the last part of 2026, with GPU volumes restarting in 2027; GPUs to be softly replaced by CPUs and ASICs in Q4, with no particular gross-margin difference but less operating leverage (more designs, more projects). Possible small H2 margin dilution from higher agency / distribution fees, labour awards and R&D / SG&A costs of the ramp-up of the new factory being built in China to serve the domestic market (EUR 3 million to EUR 4 million of ramp-up cost in H2). Turnkey solutions are the most profitable product and were very exposed in Q2; the two main GPU-related customers are the most important portion of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: China factory ramp-up cost EUR 3 million to EUR 4 million in H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stefano Felici: AI-related products (GPU, CPU, ASICs) now represent more than 50% of total revenue; he claims Technoprobe is leading the market with very strong share in each segment. H2 view: AI demand strong with no material change in momentum; consumer slight growth broadly in line with H1; automotive and industrial gradual recovery. For 2027 he does not expect major changes in the ratio between GPU, CPU and HBM. Demand driver: more AI chips to be tested and longer test time (test intensity). Management expects no margin dilution on new products (ASICs, HBM, silicon photonics) at mass volumes.

HBM (CFO): 2026 HBM revenue expected to be very small, in the range of EUR 10 million, no more; Technoprobe is qualified by one of the three customers and still in qualification with the other two main players; 2027 magnitude still to be defined and depends on customer adoption of vertical MEMS probes instead of cantilever; one customer is already using it at prototype stage. CEO: the vertical MEMS approach leverages the logic probe technology and aims for logic-level profitability.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 HBM revenue ~EUR 10 million; qualified at one of the three customers

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon photonics (CEO): the market is still in a characterization phase this year with lab-oriented solutions; Technoprobe has developed the core technology for high-volume testing, and the start of volumes will probably happen during 2027, though it is still early to predict the size of the business.

CEO: main customers were very hungry for capacity and would take any capacity available; every supplier in the industry (PCB suppliers, semiconductor machine suppliers) is short of capacity. Technoprobe owns and develops its main production equipment and the equipment software (vertical integration), which he says let it grow capacity faster than other players.
